layers.authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Nature Conservation Sector
layers.process: Visitor fee for the South Sinai protectorates (Ras Mohammed, Nabq, Taba, Abu Galum, St Catherine): foreign visitor USD 5 (about A$7.10); foreign small car up to 5 people USD 5; foreign large car over 5 people USD 10 (about A$14.20). Fees double for visits that run past sunset (camping and land or sea safaris). Children under 7 are exempt. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = USD 0.7040).

layers.authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Nature Conservation Sector
layers.process: Blue Hole area in the Abu Galum protectorate (north of Dahab): foreign visitor USD 10 (about A$14.20, RBA 30 October 2026).

layers.authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Nature Conservation Sector
layers.process: Boats in the South Sinai and Red Sea protectorates pay by length: over 17 to 20 metres USD 10; over 20 to 25 metres USD 20 (about A$28.41); over 25 to 30 metres USD 40 (about A$56.82); over 30 metres USD 60 (about A$85.23). Boats up to 17 metres are exempt. The boat operator pays this.

EEAA runs an environmental permit system for activities inside protectorates, starting (phase one) with the protectorates of South Sinai and the Red Sea. Boats, dive centres, marine activity centres, tour companies, other bodies and individuals, and temporary activities each use their own application form. Camping inside a protectorate needs approval or a permit under Law 102 of 1983 on natural protectorates. Commercial filming and photography inside a protectorate needs its own permit, with a list of required documents.

layers.authority: Local authorities, as reported by Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Smartraveller)
layers.process: Smartraveller says rules apply to people entering the Sinai, including via the Ahmed Hamdi tunnel. On entry you must present one of: a valid ID with a Sinai address; proof of ownership or a rental contract for property in the Sinai; or hard-copy evidence of a hotel booking. Travel in a 4WD vehicle in the Sinai may be restricted without a valid permit.

layers.authority: Local authorities, as reported by Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Smartraveller)
layers.process: Smartraveller (Israel page) says Australians entering Egypt at the Taba crossing without a visa in advance are stamped with a Sinai-only entry permit, allowing up to 15 days in the Sinai Peninsula. Fees are paid at the border.

zone-requirements.note: The fee page says the protectorate pages are being updated, and attaches Ministerial Decree 360 of 2025 on protectorate visiting charges, with its start postponed for Ras Mohammed, the Northern Islands, and Erg and Fanous. The decree is a scanned image and was not read, so the newer charges are not recorded. Confirm the current fee at the gate. St Catherine Monastery's own entry rules are not checked here.

laws.rule: Camping inside a protectorate in South Sinai needs approval or a permit under Law 102 of 1983 on natural protectorates. EEAA's camping conditions: follow the protectorate's instructions and staff; don't burn or bury waste, liquid or solid, at the camp; tents must be easy to take down; no camps in wadi beds (dry valley floors) or near dams; at least 100 metres between camps; no digging or building; don't pull up or damage plants; use dry toilets; fires only in set fire places; noise kept within the limits of Environment Law 4 of 1994; car horns and loudspeakers are prohibited inside the protectorate; park only where a P sign is posted; a person with a first-aid certificate is present while camping.
Commercial filming or photography inside a protectorate in South Sinai needs an EEAA permit; EEAA publishes the documents required and the environmental conditions for commercial filming.
